scope: Proposition 6.1 (Whole-plane walls and local determination) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 86-87. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: There are two signed nested wall systems O, E, coupled with J, with the following properties. (i) Each has the marginal law of a whole-plane nested CLE4. Domain means for O are even multiples of λ and its wall levels are odd multiples; E has the shifted parity. (ii) Under counting Palm measure at a loop, its two side disks carry independent Dirichlet fields with constant side data differing by 2λ, modulo the common period. The nesting on either side is the deterministic level-CLE construction of that side field. (iii) Both systems are determined by J. Under conditionally independent resampling outside an open patch with its field fixed, their arc portions within the patch, together with directions and local data, agree almost surely. This statement does not fix the outside grouping of separated arcs. 86 (iv) The two systems do not cross. If a wall has a proper open arc in one side of another wall and touches that wall, its level equals the actual mean on that side in a common real lift. For two conditionally independent copies of the same system given J, unequal loops cannot meet. All assertions about conditional resampling hold simultaneously for countably many sampled conditional extensions and countably many buffered observations.
